newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION - Lomu to be immortalised as a wax dummy.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Lomu to be immortalised as a wax dummy.

text.p: LONDON, Nov 25 - Giant All Black wing Jonah Lomu may not have entered the ranks of rugby immortals just yet, but he will soon be joining other famous figures from history as a wax dummy at Madame Tussaud's.
The famous London waxworks museum features notable figures from history, and modern times, and is one of London's most popular tourist attractions.
Lomu, currently touring England with the New Zealand Barbarians, will have a three-hour sitting with a Madame Tussaud's sculptor next week to capture the intricacies of his features.
However, Madame Tussaud's spokeswoman Vicky Brown said Lomu's dummy was earmarked for an exhibition which will tour Australia next year.
"That's not to say he won't also go on display in London," she told NZPA.
"At this stage he will be part of the tour of Australia, from October 1997.
"We will be taking around 100 figures to Australia, and it will be a mixture of the existing gallery with some newcomers pertinent to that market. He obviously comes into the latter category."
Brown said Madame Tussaud's had a committee which decided who would be immortalised in wax. They judged candidates on their contribution to history, and how much they are in the news.

Lomu is certainly news in Britain, featuring daily in reports on the New Zealand Barbarians tour. Images of him trampling his way to four tries in the 1995 World Cup semifinal against England are imprinted on the memory of every English rugby supporter.
Only one rugby player, former England captain Will Carling, is currently on display in Madame Tussaud's.
If Lomu did go on display in London, joining the likes of the Royal Family, the Beatles and Luciano Pavarotti, he would be the only New Zealander.
Brown said the Australian exhibition may also visit New Zealand, although it is still in the planning stages and no firm itinerary has been decided.
